input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Deepen (flagship 4) changepoint-detector: step-robust omega for --model drift
errors: First driftNoiseML profiled sigma with a likelihood that dropped one log sigma^2 per change (unit-dependent bonus per change) and reported a sigma one step ahead of its changes; caught when TCPD cut counts disagreed between two runs.
Second version charged that term to every point and went unbounded (sigma to 0, q at grid top); replaced by holding sigma at the lag intercept.
integrity_issues: The shipped estimator is the third version, chosen after the first version's TCPD scores and the second's TCPD q values and cut counts had been seen. The decision rule was fixed before the first run and not changed, but the TCPD figures are not a clean single pre-registered run; README and post say so.

doc_friction.issue: Flagship rows truncate `next:` at ~500 characters, so picking between flagships meant a separate yaml dump (PR #14757 is adding --venture for this).

deviations.why: The pre-registered rule's second half (beat the warning's refit on both sets) passed on the means, which would have put the drift model in the default consensus panel; not taken because every interval includes zero and the estimator was revised after seeing TCPD output.
deviations.did: Made ML wander the default for --model drift only; panel step left for fresh labelled data.
deviations.result: Headline agreed-changes line unchanged; no pinned real-series test moved.

goal: Fix the drift model's Nile miss (a step inflating the wander estimate) without losing TCPD F1.
notes: Verification: node --test drift-level.test.mjs 9/9 pass; full venture suite via run_venture_tests.py changepoint-detector (result below). TCPD eval 566 ms for 38 series. Nile no-change ML reproduces Durbin & Koopman 15,099 / 1,469.
